title: Optimal Platforms for Search and Matching
abstract: arXiv:2505.00205v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Search and matching increasingly take place on online platforms with elements of centralized and decentralized matching. Platforms can alter the search process for users, but cannot eliminate search frictions entirely. I study a model where users pay to change the distribution of potential partners they search over and characterize the revenue-maximizing platform when match characteristics are private information. With complementary match characteristics, I show that the only possible source of inefficiency on the optimal platform is exclusion, unlike standard screening problems. Matching on the optimal platform is perfectly assortative --- there is no equilibrium mismatch. This conclusion is robust to various manners in which fees are collected (e.g. subscription fees or match fees), and to environments where the platform designer can also change search speeds.

translated_title: 搜索与匹配的最优平台
translated_abstract: 搜索与匹配越来越多地发生在兼具集中式与分散式匹配要素的在线平台上。平台可以改变用户的搜索过程，但无法完全消除搜索摩擦。我研究了一个模型，其中用户付费以改变其搜索的潜在伙伴分布，并在匹配特征为私人信息的情况下刻画了收入最大化的平台。在匹配特征互补的情况下，我证明了最优平台上唯一可能的低效率来源是排斥，这与标准的筛选问题不同。最优平台上的匹配是完全同质匹配的——不存在均衡错配。这一结论对各种收费方式（如订阅费或匹配费）以及平台设计者还可以改变搜索速度的环境都是稳健的。
tldr: 该文构建了用户付费改变潜在伙伴分布的搜索匹配模型并刻画了收入最大化的最优平台，证明在匹配特征互补时最优平台实现完全同质匹配、唯一可能的低效率来源是排斥，且该结论对收费方式及可调节搜索速度的环境均稳健。
en_tdlr: This paper characterizes the revenue-maximizing platform in a search-and-matching model where users pay to alter their potential partner distribution, showing that with complementary match characteristics the optimal platform achieves perfectly assortative matching with exclusion as the only possible inefficiency, robust to fee structures and adjustable search speeds.
